findings.description: `_newest_blocked_escalate_record` treats every generationless record for a dispatch as matching any requested generation. Consequently, an explicit generation can select a generationless record, and an old legacy record can be reused after the dispatch parks at a later generation. This violates both the requirement that explicit generation select only that blocked generation and the requirement that later generations require a new decision.

The manual `escalate_resume` path rebuilds `ctx` with only five fields and omits the fixed `reason: supervised phase retry budget exhausted`. Manual and automatic resolution therefore do not use the identical six-field allowlisted context required by the specification.

`_current_parked_policy_pause_attempt` returns the first matching parked attempt in persisted list order rather than selecting or validating the newest lease generation. With more than one matching historical/current parked entry, dispatch-only answers can bind to an older generation, while an explicit current generation can be rejected before `_newest_blocked_escalate_record` is consulted.

Task 3.1 is marked complete, but the packet contains no implementation or tests for deriving the exact current unapplied delegated-batch cohort, rejecting missing or historical results before callbacks, or retaining terminal-persisted but unapplied members. The supplied production changes address only escalation routing, so completion of the delegated batch-apply requirement is not evidenced.
